one: Turn LLMs into agents that can retrieve, reason, and execute long-horizon tasks: RAG, tools, knowledge bases, formal methods, and long-range planning.
pos: CS 224V is a project-based agentic AI course with hard-core lectures, taught by Yuhao He and others. It is not about calling APIs; it systematically discusses agent reliability: reducing hallucination, mixing structured and unstructured knowledge, using formal methods to guarantee decisions, and optimizing long-horizon tasks.
topics: **RAG and task formalization**: retrieval augmentation, formal task descriptions, reducing hallucination
**Hybrid knowledge reasoning**: joint reasoning over databases, knowledge bases, and unstructured text
**AI-driven knowledge curation**: organizing and discovering knowledge in scientific discovery
**Formal methods**: improving the accuracy and interpretability of decision-making agents
**Long-horizon agents**: automatically optimizing accuracy and efficiency on long tasks
**Quarter-long project**: method research or a domain agent
prereq: One of LINGUIST 180/280, CS 124, CS 224N, CS 224S, or CS 224U.
assess: Lectures plus a quarter-long project that carries most of the grade (research or application). Check the current syllabus for details.
who: People who want to do agent research, AI scientists, or domain automation; anyone who knows LLM basics and wants to go deeper on reliability and formal guarantees.
tips: Get familiar with ReAct, Toolformer, RAG, and function calling first. Pick a quantifiable task for the project, or evaluation will be hard.
